questions.question: What does `getItemLayout` let `FlatList` skip, and what constraint makes it usable?
options: It skips rendering entirely; it requires no constraints
It skips measuring each row's position by computing it mathematically, which only works when every row has a fixed, known height
It disables virtualization entirely for better performance
questions.explanation: getItemLayout trades the ability to handle variable-height rows for avoiding per-row layout measurement, which is only valid when row height is fixed and known ahead of time.

questions.question: Why does wrapping list row components in `React.memo` tend to matter more on React Native than on the web?
options: React.memo doesn't work at all in React Native without this
Mobile devices generally have less CPU/GPU headroom than desktop browsers, so unnecessary re-renders of visible rows are more likely to visibly drop frames
FlatList requires React.memo to function at all
It has exactly the same impact on both platforms
questions.explanation: The same unnecessary re-render that's imperceptible on a powerful desktop browser can cause noticeable jank on more constrained mobile hardware.

questions.question: What is Hermes?
options: A state management library for React Native
A JavaScript engine built specifically for React Native, used in place of a general-purpose engine like JSC or V8
A testing framework for React Native apps
questions.explanation: Hermes is an engine optimized for React Native's specific needs, trading some things for faster startup and lower memory use.

questions.question: How does Hermes improve app startup time?
options: It skips running JavaScript entirely on first launch
It can precompile JavaScript to bytecode ahead of time at build, so the app doesn't need to parse and compile raw JS on every cold start
It caches API responses between launches
It reduces the number of components rendered on startup
questions.explanation: Ahead-of-time bytecode compilation removes the parse/compile step that would otherwise happen fresh on every cold app start.
